summary_paraphrase: A boy runs indoors to fetch his ball for a waiting game and finds his room too messy to search; place by place he looks and fails while, in the pictures, each place he searches ends up tidy; his friends give up and leave, and only when the room is clean does he spot the box where the ball was, and they play the next day.

beats.function: the room is clean; one box left

characters.name: Jami
characters.desire: to find his ball and play
characters.fear: losing the game and his friends' patience
characters.change: from frantic searching to a tidy room and a found ball

characters.name: the cat
characters.relation_to_protagonist: his pet, never mentioned in the text
characters.humor_source: copies his searching and his worry

humor_notes: Irony between text and picture: each 'No, it's not!' is shown over a freshly tidied corner; the cat copies Jami's every move and expression.

repetition.description: question to the reader 'Is the ball on/near …?' then the answer page 'No, it's not!'
repetition.why: the listener answers before the turn, and each answer page quietly shows a tidied place

repetition.description: 'No, it's not!' returns, the third time extended
repetition.why: a sayable answer the child can shout

repetition.description: 'Hold on!' from the opening returns when Jami calls back; the room picture from p4 returns tidy on p15
repetition.why: lets the reader see the change the text only states late

notes: The tidying is shown only in the pictures (pp6, 8, 12) until the text names it on p15.
The ball shows at the top of the box on p16 before it is found.
A cat companion, never mentioned in the text, mirrors Jami's dismay and worry (pp3, 10).
One wordless page (p14) carries his anger.

strengths: a question-answer pattern the listener can join on every turn
a hidden second story (tidying) told by the pictures and named at the turn
the child finds the ball himself; no adult
a cost that matters (friends leave) before the solution
weaknesses: 18 pages is long for the pattern; the third search adds little new
the lesson about tidying is implied, which is good, but the ending skips the friends' reaction

child_appeal_heuristic.label: Research heuristic — not validated
child_appeal_heuristic.rationale: Scores are the analyst's reading of the pages, not observations of children.

age_suitability.notes: Peak is frustration and friends leaving (research 4/5, about 2 on the engine's 0-3 scale), resolved by the child; climbing a chair to a high shelf is shown once.

metrics.lexicon_note: direct_address and sound_words are lexicon counts: a floor, not a measure. direct_address counts second-person words anywhere, dialogue included — it is not narrator-to-reader address

repetition.end_rhyme_note: heuristic: consecutive lines sharing a final two letters
